rv.q: As our 21st century world rushes toward ruin, I can’t help being grateful for living in a town that has cultivated an ensemble of actors capable of rising to the level of Shaw at his heartfelt best.
The show is funny, insightful, and moving, landing with a potent emotional wallop.

Nike Doukas does the impressive staging/pacing feat of not only keeping all ten characters distinct but also brings out all of the intelligence and cleverness of Shaw’s writing via the clarity of her direction.

Through reviving Shaw's masterwork with masterful flair, Antaeus not only faithfully resurrects the biting social satire of Shaw's era but offers us our own contemporary taste of, as Captain Shotover puts it, 'the sweetness of the fruit that is going rotten.'
This is a richly entertaining production, honoring both Shaw’s wit and his dismay at the superficiality of society.
Antaeus demonstrates that's simply not true.
Doukas trusts that gap to carry the irony, and she has cast the play superbly. She has not given them a house worth losing.

cn.t: Critics praise this lucid, stunning production of Shaw's dark comedy, highlighting Nike Doukas's direction, strong performances, and the play's resonant themes about society and class that remain frighteningly relevant today.
